title: 把你的本子弄脏了  (I Got Your Notebook Dirty)

segments.t: At lunchtime, Ji Xiu drops by Xingtian to eat with Bu Xiaogu. In the hallway she "accidentally" spills on Xiaogu's notebook — and steals a quick look at the notes inside. Listen first.
吉总，你在哪儿啊？
我是布小谷，我带您出去。
好啊，我在这儿呢。
小谷，对不起啊，把你的本子都弄脏了。
没事，没关系。
见什么都要看看，不好意思啊。
没事，那我带您去吃饭。
打扰了，那我先告辞了。
Now let's go through each line of their lunchtime encounter.
吉总，你在哪儿啊？
'President Ji, where are you?' On the phone, "ni zai nar a?" is the warmest, most natural way to ask where the other person is standing.
我是布小谷，我带您出去。
'This is Bu Xiaogu; I will take you out.' On phone calls Mandarin says "wo shi...", literally 'I am...', where English says 'this is...', followed by polite "dai nin chuqu", 'lead you out'.
好啊，我在这儿呢。
'Great — I am right over here.' Cheerful "hao a" accepts an offer warmly, and "zher" in "wo zai zher ne" is the northern spoken word for 'right here'.
小谷，对不起啊，把你的本子都弄脏了。
'Xiaogu, I am so sorry — I got your notebook all dirty.' Sincere "duibuqi" is the standard apology 'I am sorry', while "nong zang" combines catch-all "nong", 'make', with "zang", 'dirty'.
没事，没关系。
'It is fine, it does not matter.' Pair both replies to "duibuqi" in your memory: casual "meishi" ('it is nothing') and classic "mei guanxi" ('no problem, it doesn't matter').
见什么都要看看，不好意思啊。

'Whatever I see, I cannot help taking a look — sorry about that.' Notice lighter apology "bu haoyisi" here: where "duibuqi" apologises for a real spill, "bu haoyisi" excuses a small awkward habit like peeking.
没事，那我带您去吃饭。
'No worries — then let me take you to eat.' Everyday "chifan", literally 'eat rice', is the universal Chinese word for having a meal of any kind.
打扰了，那我先告辞了。

'Sorry for the intrusion — I will take my leave first.' Polite visitors say "darao le" ('sorry to have bothered you') and graceful "gaoci" when excusing themselves at the end of a visit. Now let's listen to the whole corridor encounter once more.
吉总，你在哪儿啊？
我是布小谷，我带您出去。
好啊，我在这儿呢。
小谷，对不起啊，把你的本子都弄脏了。
没事，没关系。
见什么都要看看，不好意思啊。
没事，那我带您去吃饭。
打扰了，那我先告辞了。
Xiaogu thinks nothing of the spill — not realising Ji Xiu has seen her notes. You learned the apology pair "duibuqi" and "mei guanxi", plus "chifan" and polite "darao le".
